title: I built a "what am I signing?" checker for Solana in a weekend
summary:
Most people approve crypto transactions blind. A site says "Claim your airdrop!", the wallet pops up, you click Approve... and hope.

Wallet drainers count on that. One common Solana trick doesn't even "send" your tokens. It quietly hands ownership of your token account to the attacker. No obvious transfer, just gone.

So for the MLH Solana Hackathon I built Clear Sign: paste a transaction (or click a button on a dApp) and see what it will really do before you sign.

summary:
Delivery app, real estate site, store locator: sooner or later, a project in Tunisia needs a base map. And not just any map. People expect to see their neighbourhood, their street names and the road numbers they actually drive on.

title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
summary:
datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages

I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table.

This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this:

link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next"

title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
summary:
Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
summary:
Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed.

By Sergio De Simone

summary:

title: Arc Browser in 2026: Worth Leaving Chrome For?
summary:
Arc Browser has been called the Chrome replacement we've been waiting for. Its workspace-and-spaces model is the most significant rethink of browser UI in years. But innovation doesn't automatically mean better. Here is where the approach holds up, where it gets in the way, and who should actually switch.

Quick Verdict

Arc Browser (2026) is the most innovative desktop browser available today — if you're on a Mac. Its Spaces-based tab management, auto-archive, and split-view completely rethink how we organize our browsing life. The learning curve is real, and the Windows version is still catching up, but for knowledge workers drowning in tabs, Arc is a revelation.

Overall Rating: 8/10 Target audience: Mac-based power users, project jugglers, and tab hoarders.

title: Wholesale prices for tagged customers on Shopify, without a second store
summary:
A lot of small Shopify stores end up with a few wholesale buyers almost by accident: a café that wants your coffee by the case, a boutique that resells your candles, a gym that orders shakers in bulk. They shouldn't pay retail, but setting up a whole B2B operation for five accounts feels like overkill.

This post walks through the usual options, what each one is good and bad at, and a simple setup based on customer tags. I'm writing it as AppVerix, a small studio that makes Shopify apps (one of them does this, mentioned at the end), but the first part applies whatever you end up using.

The four common approaches

1. A separate wholesale store. Clean separation, but you now maintain two catalogs, two inventories (or a sync app), two themes and usually two subscriptions. For a handful of buyers, that's a lot of upkeep.

title: 監視カメラが「見張る」時代に、VRが「見る力」を取り戻す理由
summary:
監視カメラが「見張る」時代に、VRが「見る力」を取り戻す理由

英国政府が交通ハブや公共イベントでライブ顔認証（LFR）を導入し、史上最大規模の移民取り締まりに活用する——という報道が流れました。同じ「目」の技術が、誰かを監視するためではなく、本人の視覚を支えるために使えないか。エンジニアとして、この非対称性は無視できません。

正直に言えば、最初は懐疑的でした。昨年の秋、友人の娘さん（7歳）が弱視と診断され、週に一度の通院と自宅での遮蔽訓練に親子ともども疲れ果てていると聞いた夜のことです。彼女は片眼をアイパッチで覆われたまま、じっとテレビを見るのが苦痛で、すぐに外してしまう。「この子が好きな動画を、そのまま見ながら訓練できたら」——その素朴な願いが、技術の使い道を考え直すきっかけになりました。

Seven Sportsが開発したMeta Questアプリ「Amblyotube」は、その問いへのひとつの実装です。設計の核は、VRヘッドセットが本質的に持つ「2つの独立したアイピース」というハードウェア特性。左右それぞれに別の映像フィードを送れるため、YouTubeのストリーミングをそのままデュオプティック（dichoptic）トレーニングへ変換できます。既存の動画資産をそのまま訓練装置に変える、という発想がまず面白い。

アーキテクチャ上のポイントは3つ。第一に、優位眼側へ調整可能なブラー・コントラスト・不透明度をかける「Dominant Eye Shader」で、100%にすると完全なデジタル遮蔽として機能します。第二に、AIが動画内の人物（顔・身体）を検出し、弱視眼側の映像だけに選択的シャープニングをかける「Lazy Eye Sharpener（MFBFモード）」。第三に、両眼競合を減らす「Wedge Occlusion」——各眼の視野の一部を黒く塗り、それぞれが異なる領域を見る状態を作ります。

融像の練習には「Magenta Focus Cue」を使います。自然な映像の肌色・緑・青に対して高いコントラストを持つマゼンタを弱視眼に、控えめなグレーを優位眼に提示し、脳に2つの信号を統合させる。地味ですが、色選択の設計としては合理的です。

title: How to Give Claude, Cursor or Any AI Agent a Voice: Voiceovers and Subtitles with an MCP Server
summary:
You asked Claude to write a 60-second script for your next video. It did, in seconds. Then you copied the text into a text-to-speech website, downloaded an MP3, opened a subtitle editor, typed timings by hand, and dragged three files into your video editor. The AI wrote the words, but you still did all the production work.

The missing piece is a voice: a way for the agent itself to turn text into audio files and matching subtitles. This tutorial shows how to add one to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client using an open-source MCP server.

title: I built a new programming language with a built-in 3D engine (Built with Rust)
summary:
Hey Dev.to community! 👋

For the past year, I’ve been working on a solo project that started as a frustration with game development setup. I love Rust, but sometimes setting up a new game project with OpenGL and various dependencies takes hours before you even draw a single pixel.

So, I decided to build my own solution. Meet Venk — a modern, high-performance programming language designed specifically for 2D/3D game development.

Today, I am thrilled to announce the first public release: Venk Beta v0.0.1! 🚀
🤔 What is Venk?

Venk is a completely independent language (written in Rust) with its own Lexer, Parser, and Interpreter. But unlike Python or GDScript, Venk comes with batteries included.
